## TL;DR

Ran the Hub Dev app (`org.repoos.mobile.dev`) on the Pixel 8 Android 16 (API 36) emulator after the saved wireless phone endpoint refused connection. The emulator was available through the installed Android SDK even though `emulator` was not on `PATH`. I built and installed only the debug/dev variant. The pass found and fixed two app defects: URL validation text did not clear after a URL was entered, and failed biometric authentication unlocked the picker. Both fixes have regression tests. I also filed #1166 for dark-mode status icons that are almost invisible on Android 16's light status-bar strip, attaching the emulator screenshot.

The pass exercised the picker, Add server, edit/remove sheet, Settings, all eight themes in Light and Dark, the no-trusted-server discovery state, opening an external web page, returning with Android's back gesture, and both lock failure and success states. The biometric rejection and successful retry paths were both exercised after enrolling a synthetic emulator fingerprint. Discovery against a reachable trusted RepoOS server remains unverified because the candidate server endpoint was unreachable.

## Work and rationale

I checked the active task and board using RepoOS, confirmed the worktree was clean, and rechecked ADB. There was no phone attached. `avdmanager list avd` showed the `tuk-pixel` Pixel 8 AVD, and Android SDK packages included an API 36 Google APIs image and emulator binary under the Homebrew Android command-line-tools directory. I launched that AVD, waited for `emulator-5554` to appear, built with `just build-android`, and installed `mobile/app-debug.apk`. Package inspection confirmed only `org.repoos.mobile.dev` was installed for Hub. I did not run `just deploy-phone` because the saved phone port was unavailable.

I captured each screen with `adb exec-out screencap -p` and visually inspected the PNGs. Picker evidence includes the empty state (`server-list.png`) and a seeded one-server list (`server-list-seeded.png`, final rebuild `server-list-final.png`). The Add server screen is `add-server.png`; an empty Save attempt is `add-server-empty-error.png`; the stale message remaining after typing was captured before the fix in `add-server-filled.png`. After the fix, `add-server-error-cleared.png` shows the entered URL with no stale missing-URL message. A live attempt to add `https://dev.repoos.org` returned “Unreachable”; I did not treat that URL as a usable RepoOS server.

The missing-URL defect came from `App.vue`: the error was cleared on submit but not while the URL input changed. I added `errorAfterServerUrlInput`, wired it to URL input, and tested that nonblank input clears the error while whitespace-only input retains it. Both cases pass.

To exercise list interactions without pretending a remote server was available, I seeded two synthetic entries into the emulator's app-local Capacitor preferences. I opened the edit sheet (`edit-server.png`), used Delete and confirmed the remaining card (`remove-server.png`), then opened `https://example.org` (`server-open.png`). The page loaded in the native in-app browser. An Android edge back gesture returned to the picker (`server-back-gesture.png`). The interaction worked; logcat emitted Chromium `Renderer process crash detected (code -1)` as the browser renderer was torn down. The app remained in the picker. I recorded this as a teardown log message, not a reproduced user-visible app crash.

Settings was checked in Light (`settings-light.png`) and Dark (`settings-dark-final.png`). The theme selector contains Classic, Clear, Gen Z, Jelly, Gruvbox, Catppuccin, Solarized and Hypercolor. I captured and inspected a separate Settings screenshot for each theme in each appearance mode: `theme-<theme>-light.png` and `theme-<theme>-dark.png` for all eight names. Text and controls remained visible and no clipping or overlap appeared in those captures. Dark-mode screenshots show Android 16's status icons rendered in white against a light system status-bar strip. Since the status-bar background API is ignored for target SDK 36, a trial enabling WebView overlay caused a Capacitor safe-area injection error and a blank view; I reverted that experiment. I filed #1166 with the dark-theme screenshot and the platform-specific reproduction details.

I enabled the app lock and restarted the app. The emulator reports “No fingerprints enrolled”; before the fix, that authentication rejection dismissed the overlay and left the picker available. I changed `gateLock` so failed verification keeps the overlay open and added a “Try again” action. The final capture `lock-fail-closed-final.png` shows the locked screen after the repeated plugin rejection. I added tests for both the failed and successful verification overlay states. I enrolled a synthetic fingerprint in the AVD and verified that a successful retry closed the lock overlay and returned to the picker (`lock-unlocked.png`).

Tailnet discovery was opened from the empty picker and captured at `tailnet-discovery.png`. It correctly explains that a trusted server must be added first and offers the manual URL action. Discovery through a trusted server was not tested because the only attempted endpoint was unreachable. The lock setting and About content remained visible in Settings; no overlapping or clipped controls were observed.

## Approaches tried

- Checked the saved wireless phone through ADB; no device was attached, so I used the existing Pixel 8 AVD rather than claiming phone evidence.
- Used the dev debug APK only; no release APK was installed.
- Used synthetic local server records to reach edit, remove and open flows without misrepresenting a successful server connection.
- Tried status-bar overlay mode to make the dark theme color extend behind Android 16's status bar. The resulting safe-area injection error and blank app view made that approach unsuitable, so I reverted it and filed #1166 for a focused platform-aware fix.
- Ran the mobile TypeScript/Vite build and the targeted Vitest file after the small fixes; all four regression assertions passed.

## Challenges and blockers

The real phone endpoint remains unavailable, so all native evidence is from the Pixel 8 emulator. I enrolled a synthetic fingerprint in the AVD after the initial lock failure-path pass. That enabled verification of both rejected authentication remaining locked and successful biometric retry returning to the picker. The tailnet screen was checked only in its no-trusted-server state; no server returned discovery rows. Human follow-up #1162 exists, is assigned to a human and depends on #1159. I narrowed it to the remaining live discovery proof and put it on hold until a reachable trusted RepoOS server is available.

A dark status-bar contrast issue remains open as #1166 with an attached emulator screenshot. The experimental overlay path was reverted, and the regular Hub screen layout was rebuilt and checked afterwards. No changes were made to `repoos.toml`.

## Key learnings

A configured AVD can make a blocked device pass possible even when the emulator executable is missing from `PATH`; `avdmanager` and the installed SDK image identified the usable setup. Synthetic app-local preferences are useful for driving presentation and navigation states, but they do not prove connectivity, tailnet results or a valid RepoOS sign-in. An authentication rejection must leave protected UI covered, while still exposing an explicit retry. Android 16's enforced edge-to-edge behavior also means native status-bar color changes need to be verified against the actual target SDK, not inferred from the app's CSS theme. The remaining external-state proof is discovery rows from a reachable trusted RepoOS server. Emulator biometric success is captured in `lock-unlocked.png`; it does not validate a real phone fingerprint sensor.
